title: .NET 11 MAUI Preview 7 Adds Passkeys, Incremental XAML Hot Reload, and Shell Route Templates to MAUI
gist: .NET 11 Preview 7 delivers a substantial MAUI update: cross-platform passkey authentication in MAUI Essentials, a new incremental XAML Hot Reload enabled by default for Debug, ASP.NET-style Shell route templates, expanded AOT-safe bindings, and continued migration from legacy renderers to handlers on Apple platforms.

insights.claim: MAUI Preview 7 adds a Passkeys API in MAUI Essentials driving native passkey experiences on Android 14+, iOS/Mac Catalyst 16+ and supported Windows 10, with CreateAsync, AssertAsync and IsSupported, while deliberately leaving relying-party server responsibilities to the application.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Native cross-platform passkeys let MAUI apps adopt passwordless auth, a security and UX upgrade for mobile developers.

insights.claim: XAML Incremental Hot Reload arrives as a preview enabled by default for Debug builds, combining a source generator with MetadataUpdateHandler to modify already-created pages rather than rebuilding XAML wholesale, handling property changes, adding/removing children, reordering, bindings and ResourceDictionary changes, and working with dotnet watch.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Faster, more capable hot reload directly improves MAUI developer iteration speed.

insights.claim: Shell navigation gains route templates modeled on ASP.NET Core and Blazor routing supporting required, optional, default, constrained, catch-all and mixed segments like product/{sku}, though template routes currently support only absolute navigation, not relative.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Familiar web-style routing lowers the learning curve for MAUI navigation, with a noted relative-navigation limitation.
insights.locator: Shell navigation gains route templates paragraph

insights.claim: The XAML source generator expanded AOT work so {RelativeSource AncestorType=...} bindings compile to trim-safe TypedBinding instances when the ancestor type resolves at compile time, avoiding reflection-based string paths, while Self and TemplatedParent still use the runtime path.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: More trim-safe bindings advance MAUI's Native AOT readiness, improving app size and startup.
insights.locator: The XAML source generator has also expanded paragraph

insights.claim: Preview 7 exposes new extension points for third-party platform backends, with OnPlatform recognizing GTK, macOS and WPF and infrastructure like alert, gesture and BlazorWebView exposing contracts external backends can implement through NuGet packages instead of patching MAUI.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Opening backend contracts lets third parties extend MAUI to new platforms without maintaining forks.
insights.locator: Preview 7 exposes new extension points paragraph

insights.claim: The renderer-to-handler migration continues on Apple platforms, with NavigationPage and TabbedPage now using handlers by default on iOS and Mac Catalyst, while compatibility renderers remain available as manual fallbacks so apps with custom renderers should test before adopting broadly.
insights.speaker: Edin Kapić
insights.so_what: Handler-by-default is a migration milestone that carries upgrade-testing risk for apps with custom renderers.
